channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Top 10 African countries that made the most money from the United States last year
item.description: Last year, African imports from the United States increased, reflecting stronger economic linkages, diversity of demand, and altering global supply chains.

item.title: Gold rush tragedy in Guinea as mine collapses, leaving workers trapped and injured
item.description: At least one person has died, and several others were injured after an artisanal gold mine collapsed near Kintinian, about 25 kilometres from Siguiri in northeastern Guinea, according to local authorities and witnesses.

item.title: 10 African countries with the fewest rocket projectors in 2026
item.description: The security situation in Africa in 2026 is still heavily influenced by outside forces, and as a result, high-end weapons systems like rocket projectors can come in very handy.

item.title: US, UK, China investors on alert as Nigeria rolls out $750 million mini-grid solar initiative
item.description: Nigeria has launched an ambitious $750 million renewable electrification programme aimed at expanding electricity access through solar mini-grids and off-grid power systems, a move officials say could unlock over $1.1 billion in private investment and reshape the country’s energy landscape.

item.title: Debt-burdened Senegal set to shut down 19 state agencies to save $98 million
item.description: Senegal has announced plans to close 19 government agencies, a move expected to save around 55 billion CFA francs ($97.95 million) over the next three years, the government said.

item.title: South African billionaire Patrice Motsepe joins race to build Africa’s next manganese export facility.
item.description: South African billionaire Patrice Motsepe is strengthening his mining empire as African Rainbow Minerals (ARM) confirmed its participation in a bid to develop a new manganese export facility at Ngqura Port in the Eastern Cape.

item.title: Ghana eyes new route as UAE flight disruptions threaten gold shipments - sources say
item.description: Ghana is exploring alternative export routes for its gold shipments amid persistent tensions in the Middle East, which threaten to disrupt flights to the United Arab Emirates, sources reveal.

item.title: Kenya is tracking a vital fuel tanker from the Middle East as East Africa braces for supply shocks
item.description: Africa’s fuel-importing economies are increasingly on edge as the U.S.- and Israel-led war with Iran threatens global oil supply routes, forcing countries such as Kenya to closely monitor tanker movements while South Africa prepares motorists for higher pump prices..

item.title: Africa's most valuable airline loses $137 million over Middle East war
item.description: Africa’s largest and most valuable airline, Ethiopian Airlines, says it has lost roughly $137 million in a single week as the escalating conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran disrupts air travel across the Middle East.

item.title: Dangote Cement sells 10% of Senegal subsidiary to government
item.description: Senegal has increased its participation in the country’s industrial sector by acquiring a 10 per cent stake in Dangote Cement’s local subsidiary, the nation’s leading cement producer.
